tagline: A hands-on, role-based curriculum for professionals who work alongside AI: directing models and agents, checking their output, and redesigning the work around them.
overview: This org covers **AI in everyday professional work**: *working alongside* the models. It's for engineers, analysts, product managers, and managers whose job isn't building AI but whose work now runs through it: delegating to coding agents and assistants, briefing them well, verifying what comes back, and building team habits that make AI-assisted work fast and safe. Every role track has a paired **learning** repository (modules, lecture chapters, exercises, quizzes) and a **solutions** repository with reference walkthroughs.
highlights: 🧭 **Judgment over tooling:** delegation, briefing, verification, and accountability, the skills that outlast any one tool
🛠️ Hands-on with real coding agents, assistants, and analysis tools, with every exercise graded on the quality of the *result*

focus.ai-assisted-software-engineer: Delegating to coding agents, writing specs & context, reviewing AI-written code, testing as verification, repo harnesses
focus.ai-augmented-analyst: AI-assisted analysis & SQL, checking generated numbers, notebook agents, reproducibility, communicating uncertainty
focus.ai-augmented-product-manager: AI in discovery & specs, prototyping with agents, judging AI output quality, PRDs as context, shipping faster safely
focus.ai-augmented-team-manager: Redesigning team workflows, review norms for AI-made work, measuring real productivity, skills & career growth
focus.ai-enablement-lead: Org-wide AI adoption: tool selection, usage policy, training programs, champions networks, measuring impact

technologies.Coding agents: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot
technologies.Analysis: Jupyter, SQL, spreadsheets with AI assistance
technologies.Context & tooling: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, Model Context Protocol (MCP), skills & hooks
technologies.Governance: Acceptable-use policies, NIST AI RMF, data-handling rules
